acceptance_criteria.details: 4 typed slices: projects, features, sessions, UI. Each slice uses StateCreator pattern with generics. Store combines slices in create() with devtools middleware.
All setter actions use type-safe parameters. setProjects(projects: Project[]), setSelectedProject(id: string | null). Build succeeds, all types validated.

Curried selector pattern: selectProjectById(id)(state). selectFeaturesByStatus(status)(state). selectActiveSessions(state) filters sessions by status. Memoization via factory pattern prevents unnecessary re-renders.

devtools middleware wraps store with {name: 'NomosStore'}. Action labels on all setters: 'projects/setProjects', 'features/setFeatureStatusFilter', etc. DevTools displays action history and state transitions.

reasons.F020: React web app provides route components and UI layout that will consume the store via useAppStore hook

discoveries.discovery: Zustand slice pattern with StateCreator generics provides excellent type safety
discoveries.context: Each slice uses StateCreator<AppStore, middleware[], empty[], SliceType> to create typed slices that compose into main store. Devtools middleware specified in type params.
discoveries.lesson: StateCreator pattern enforces type safety at compile time. Generics prevent accidental state mutations or incorrect types between slices.
discoveries.benefit: Full TypeScript support from slice definition through store consumer components

discoveries.discovery: Devtools action labels require third parameter to set() function
discoveries.context: F022 initial tests used plain strings for setter actions instead of branded types (ProjectIdSchema.parse()). Tests passed but revealed issue: mock data validation skipped.
discoveries.lesson: Mock data in tests must validate against actual Zod schemas. Test types should match production types exactly.
discoveries.issue_found: Mock projects used id: string, should use id: ProjectIdSchema.parse('P001')
discoveries.prevention: Always validate mock data with Zod schemas in tests. Use branded types from @nomos-ai/types

discoveries.discovery: Web tsconfig needs to exclude __tests__ directory when using bun:test
discoveries.context: Initial implementation placed tests in apps/web/src/store/__tests__/store.test.ts. Type checking failed because tsconfig.json had 'bun/bun' in types array, but test files couldn't find bun:test types.
discoveries.lesson: When creating test files in web package with bun:test, exclude __tests__ from typeCheck via tsconfig exclude pattern.
discoveries.fix_applied: Updated apps/web/tsconfig.json: added '__tests__/**' to exclude array
discoveries.prevention: Update tsconfig.json exclude before creating test files with bun:test. Or place tests outside src/ directory.

discoveries.discovery: Curried selector pattern for optimal memoization
discoveries.context: F022 selectors use factory pattern: selectProjectById = (id) => (state) => state.projects.find(...). Consumed as selectProjectById(id)(getState()) in components.
discoveries.lesson: Curried selectors enable memoization at selector creation time, not state lookup time. Perfect for Zustand which doesn't have built-in selector memoization like Redux.
discoveries.code_pattern: const selectProjectById = (id: string) => (state: AppStore) => state.projects.find((p) => p.id === id);
discoveries.benefit: Components can memoize selector results if passed same ID, preventing re-renders

discoveries.discovery: Feature type from @nomos-ai/types lacks projectId field
discoveries.context: During test mock creation, Feature type doesn't include projectId field even though database schema has it. Feature is API/frontend type without database-only fields.
discoveries.lesson: Zod schemas evolve separately from database schema. Frontend types intentionally exclude DB-only fields (like projectId which is only on backend Feature type from database query results).
discoveries.rationale: API contracts separate frontend concerns from database schema. Frontend Feature doesn't need to know about projectId relationship - that's fetched separately via featureId key.
discoveries.prevention: Check @nomos-ai/types schema definitions before creating mock data. DB-returned types may differ from API types.

discoveries.discovery: All 4 ACs met on first try with zero retries
discoveries.context: Feature completed with no failed tests, no type errors, all 22 tests passing on first run. Store creation pattern from Zustand docs applied correctly.
discoveries.lesson: Standard Zustand patterns are well-documented and reliable. Following the slice + devtools middleware pattern exactly works first time.
discoveries.confidence: HIGH - Zustand is battle-tested for this use case

new_patterns.name: ZUSTAND_SLICE_PATTERN
new_patterns.description: Zustand store composition using StateCreator slice pattern with devtools middleware
new_patterns.recommendation: For all frontend state management: use Zustand with slice pattern. Each domain gets its own slice combining related state and actions. Compose slices in main store with devtools middleware.
new_patterns.code_example: const createProjectsSlice: StateCreator<AppStore, [["zustand/devtools", never]], [], ProjectsSlice> = (set) => ({ projects: [], setProjects: (p) => set({projects: p}, undefined, 'projects/setProjects') });
benefits: Type-safe state management with full TypeScript support
Clean separation of concerns (projects, features, sessions, UI)
DevTools debugging with action labels and state snapshots
Composable architecture scales as app grows
new_patterns.risk_if_ignored: MEDIUM - without patterns, state management becomes scattered and hard to debug

new_patterns.name: ZUSTAND_CURRIED_SELECTORS
new_patterns.description: Selector pattern with currying for memoization in Zustand
new_patterns.recommendation: For selectors that filter or compute state: use curried pattern (id) => (state) => {...}. Enables memoization at selector creation time.
new_patterns.code_example: const selectProjectById = (id: string) => (state: AppStore) => state.projects.find(p => p.id === id);
benefits: Components can memoize results when selector ID unchanged
Prevents unnecessary re-renders in consumer components
Factory pattern creates new selector instances per query
new_patterns.risk_if_ignored: LOW - without pattern, unnecessary re-renders on state changes

code_quality_notes.type_safety: Full type safety: StateCreator generics, AppStore composition type, all selectors fully typed with return types. No 'any' types.
code_quality_notes.architectural_clarity: Clean separation: each slice self-contained with own interface, store composition straightforward, selectors well-organized
code_quality_notes.test_coverage: 22 comprehensive tests covering all slices, selectors, and devtools integration. Tests validate initial state, state updates, filter operations.
code_quality_notes.performance: Curried selectors enable memoization, devtools middleware minimal overhead, store creation once at app startup
code_quality_notes.maintainability: Adding new slice or selector requires minimal boilerplate. Clear patterns for others to follow.

architectural_insights.state_organization: Slice-based organization separates concerns. Projects, Features, Sessions, UI each have isolated state and actions. Composable design.
architectural_insights.selector_strategy: Curried selectors provide factory pattern for memoization. selectProjectById(id)(state) creates new selector per ID, enabling React.useMemo optimization.
architectural_insights.middleware_integration: DevTools middleware provides excellent debugging. Action labels ('projects/setProjects') show state transitions in DevTools.
architectural_insights.api_integration: Store ready for API integration - setters (setProjects, setFeatures) can be called after fetching from server
architectural_insights.scalability: Architecture scales well - new slices can be added without modifying core store logic. Selector pattern extensible.
